findings.finding: The child's spec is empty and neither it nor the root spec has an Acceptance section, so no phase has an acceptance line to cite in a proof's `criterion` field.
findings.answer: plan.md quotes the root spec LEGSMOKE-955 verbatim as the governing ask, reads 'this issue' as the child key (every marker names the issue whose branch added it; the driver addressed this child with 'the one-file smoke change'), and authors C1–C4 with command, expected output and negative control; proof entries cite C1/C2/C3 by label. specDepartures is [] because the plan builds the root spec's design unchanged; the architect is told the child's spec is empty.

findings.finding: 'A single line that names this issue' is not byte-defined; the key, the full title with the /tmp fixture suffix, or the precedent form give different files, and the Dispatch title can change before implementation.
findings.answer: D2 pins path smoke/LEGSMOKE-958.md and the literal 'LEGSMOKE-958: Upgrade rehearsal fallback child' + one LF (47 bytes, no CR/BOM/trailing space), derived by the repository rule <KEY>: <title minus fixture suffix>. The literal is authoritative; every role recomputes the sha1 from the bytes it reads. The implementer re-reads the title before writing and escalates to the architect if it changed.

findings.finding: The optional second line names no trigger, channel, text or cap; a second ask would silently double scope, and an append creates a new code head needing re-proof.
findings.answer: D5: trigger is a GitHub review or review thread on this PR asking for one more line in the file, or a targeted driver Dispatch message (the proof's deployment instructions); not a bare PR comment, untargeted Dispatch comment or Envoy message. Text is the review's words, default precedent 'Legion proof review round 1 (LEGSMOKE)' (K=1: 86 bytes, sha1 0776b04d…, recomputed for any other text). Cap one line; anything else goes to the architect. On K=1 the implementer re-proves C1–C3 at the new head, updates E2E/Size, rewrites implement.json; tester and reviewer repeat.

findings.finding: 'Nothing else changes' collides with the .legion/<issue>/*.json handoffs Legion commits mid-run and with retro's default docs/solutions/ learning file, which would land a second path on main after approval.
findings.answer: D4: the measurement before the READY head uses select(startswith(".legion/") | not); at the READY head and after the merge the .legion/ count must be 0 (C2b, C4); this is not a departure because nothing under .legion/ reaches main. D6: retro commits the removal only and puts the learning in its Dispatch message (allowed by skill://legion-retro); admitting a learning file is the architect's scope call.

findings.finding: Which heads carry check-runs and which head the merge gate judges is counter-intuitive: handoff-only heads show zero runs and BLOCKED, and a READY built before the gate check-run exists would be refused.
findings.answer: D7 maps the heads: code heads (marker, append, retro removal) carry four runs each; handoff heads carry total_count 0 and BLOCKED by design; no role pushes to start CI. The merger reads check-runs at the retro head once and builds READY once a gate entry exists (the daemon waits on a running check and refuses a missing one); a refusal is reported to the architect.

findings.finding: The production-like proof surface before and after the merge was unnamed, the ?ref=main 404 control dies at the merge, and a tester could reach for .fail-me as a break attempt.
findings.answer: D9/C1/C4: implementer proves on the contents API at the code head; tester independently on the git-objects API (commit → tree → blob). Absence control pinned to the planning base cfc67393… (survives the merge) plus pre-merge main with its SHA, each calibrated by smoke/LEGSMOKE-950.md → 200/59 bytes. Post-merge: merge commit file list, cmp at M, .legion/ 404 at M, recorded in the PR body, one PR comment with the footer, and a dispatch message. Creating .fail-me or any file as a break attempt is forbidden.

findings.finding: Concrete values of the precedent PR #725 (59 bytes, blob ee12d2c1…, heads, run ids, base 87eeef5a, 'beside the four tree-2 precedents') do not transfer, and this marker has no title twin.
findings.answer: D12: every SHA, run id, PR number, byte count and sibling reference is read live; 958's values are 47 bytes, blob ae7da8d2…, base cfc67393…, no cohort. The twin control is the key-sharing sibling smoke/LEGSMOKE-950.md (differ at char 12) and wrong-key literals LEGSMOKE-959/LEGSMOKE-955 (C1(b), C1(c)).

findings.finding: The planning facts cited branches/main/protection → 403, which is not the endpoint merge-gate.md prescribes; carrying it as the procedure's result could stall or mislead the reviewer.
findings.answer: D8 records the two prescribed reads, both run at planning as the review App: rules/branches/main → ruleset 24471196 requires gate only (non-strict); branches/main .protection.required_status_checks.checks → none (protected: true, checks: []). The /protection 403 is noted as outside the procedure. A refused prescribed read at review time goes to the architect and blocks approval.

findings.finding: The two blob sha1s rest on a git hash-object run the analyst could not reproduce, and the K=1 second line was not spelled out.
findings.answer: D2/D5 spell out both literals in full beside their sha1s, declare the literal authoritative and the sha1 derived, and require each role to recompute sha1('blob <n>\0' + bytes) from what it reads; a clean cmp with a disagreeing sha1 is a discrepancy report, not a failed criterion. The planner verified every pinned cmp output in the workspace.

findings.finding: Nothing recorded whether the root spec LEGSMOKE-955 is registered and approved at a version; an unapproved design gate refuses every READY in the tree.
findings.answer: D11 records the precondition as unverified by the planner (read_record shows no gate state) and routes a design-gate READY refusal to the architect verbatim; the merger does not retry on its own.

findings.finding: The driver's message names only 'the plan handoff', while the planner artifact is plan.json and the issue's plan.md document; downstream phases cite the plan by decision and criterion number.
findings.answer: Delivered: dispatch://LEGSMOKE-958/artifact/plan-md (numbered D1–D14, C1–C4, per-role ordering) and this plan.json with schemaVersion/phase/issue/completed, requiredSkills, gapAnalysis, planReview and specDepartures, committed as one handoff-only commit pushed with the skip-checks trailer, which also creates legion/LEGSMOKE-958 on origin.
